name: shadow-earth-066, earth dahu
iocPatterns: In-memory execution of DLLs via direct NT calls
HTA files used for script-based delivery
recommendedActions: Patch WinRAR software immediately to address CVE-2025-8088.
Implement endpoint detection to identify and block in-memory DLL loading via NT syscalls.
Monitor and block unauthorized HTA file executions within the corporate environment.
Audit C&C traffic for high volumes of RC4 encrypted data reaching unknown domains.
Inspect network logs for suspicious interactions with Cloudflare Workers from internal assets.
Implement strict controls on the execution of scripts and web-based application files.
Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all critical systems to mitigate stolen credential risks.
Develop an automated alert system for unauthorized access to sensitive documents across common Office extensions.
campaignsText: The campaigns involving Shadow-earth-066 and Earth Dahu exhibit a pattern of persistent exploitation over a sustained period. Both actors have been observed targeting Ukrainian infrastructure in the government, defense, financial-services, and mining sectors from late 2025 through early 2026. While they share the CVE-2025-8088 exploit for initial access, their tactical divergence—Shadow-earth-066 using C++ and RC4; Earth Dahu using HTA and Cloudflare Workers—suggests a diversified threat actor ecosystem aiming to maximize operational success against Ukrainian targets.
description: Shadow-earth-066 and Earth Dahu are Russia-aligned threat actors targeting high-value sectors in Ukraine, including government, defense, and finance. They leverage a WinRAR path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2025-8088) to deploy sophisticated information stealers and espionage modules for credential theft and data exfiltration.
goals: The actors' primary objectives are intelligence gathering and credential harvesting within strategic sectors in Ukraine. By targeting government, defense, mining, and financial services components, they aim to gain access to sensitive internal communications, state secrets, and economic data. The overlap between the two campaigns suggests a coordinated effort by Russian-aligned entities to destabilize or gather intelligence from Ukrainian infrastructure, using common entry points while diversifying their technical toolset to maximize reach.
